clue.text: Scottish king to plunder English, right?

parts.note: to plunder is to rob

explanation.surface: A question about whether raiding the English was a fair thing for a Scottish monarch to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert the Bruce is the best-known Scottish king of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Scottish monarchs bore this name, most famously Robert the Bruce.

clue.text: Puzzles? Publishes again, say, involving book

indicators.note: involving means the outer word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: publishing material a second time is an example of using it again

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether reprinting a book counts as a kind of puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the phrase as an example, not an exact synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture puzzles of letters and images are this; the question mark flags a specific type.

clue.text: It's a place to try out revolutionary British cooking

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a laboratory is where things are tested, shortened to lab

explanation.surface: A test kitchen boasting of radical new British food.
explanation.walkthrough: This curry style was developed in Birmingham, so 'British cooking' is fair despite its South Asian roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish and its cooking style originated in Birmingham's curry houses, making it British cuisine.

clue.text: No artistic movement's source perturbed follower of artistic movement

indicators.note: perturbed means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order
a word's source is its first letter, taken here from movement's

explanation.surface: A troubled adherent of some art movement denies there is any such movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' gives M, the first letter of movement's; NOARTISTIC plus M is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent of Romanticism, the arts movement of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Mother's ready to receive energy from particle

indicators.note: to receive means the outer letters take the other piece inside

parts.note: mother is mum, plus the S of the possessive
E is the physics symbol for energy
on means ready or willing, as in game on

explanation.surface: A mother gets ready to take in energy from some tiny particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' as ON is the sense of being up for something, as in 'you're on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mu-meson is the old name for the muon, a subatomic particle.

clue.text: Changed a tense? Not enthusiastic about that

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a muted response is lukewarm, not enthusiastic
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone altered a verb tense and is unimpressed by the result.
explanation.walkthrough: A and T sit inside MUTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has mutated has altered in form, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Damage horse with docking

indicators.note: docking means cutting off the tail, here the last letter

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse is harmed by having its tail cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Docking is literally cutting a horse's tail, so the surface and the device match neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or impair something is a straight synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Layperson?

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad, so a lay-person is one who makes them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Layperson' usually means a non-expert; read as lay-person it is someone who writes lays, i.e. songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of songs crafts lays, the poetic word for songs or ballads.

clue.text: Agreement about working a year or twelve

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the next

parts.note: a nod signals agreement
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Reaching an agreement on working a year, or perhaps twelve of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve' means twelve o'clock, midday, not the number of months.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, the middle of the day.

clue.text: Canadian writer strives to to follow American lawyer

indicators.note: to follow puts the striving word after the lawyer

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
to vie is to strive or compete

explanation.surface: A Canadian author works hard to keep up with a US attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'to' twice; one is a slip and serves only as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Robertson Davies was a celebrated Canadian novelist, author of the Deptford Trilogy.

clue.text: Reduction in size I intend to get back, fixing eating disorder

indicators.note: reduction means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: bulk means size or volume

indicators.note: to get back means the word runs in reverse

parts.note: to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone planning to regain weight lost by cutting back, as a way of curing an eating disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: BULK loses K; AIM reversed gives MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition marked by bingeing and purging, a recognised illness about food.

clue.text: City aware of being behind hill

indicators.note: being behind places this piece after the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
to be on to someone is to be aware of what they are doing

explanation.surface: A city realises it lies on the far side of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hilltop of south-west England, such as those on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's largest city, the capital of Ontario.

clue.text: French company isn't perturbed, though involved in endless criticism regarding experimental process?

indicators.note: involved in means these pieces go inside the outer word
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: stick means criticism, as in giving someone stick
Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

indicators.note: perturbed means upset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French firm stays calm under a barrage of criticism about its lab methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perturbed' acts only on isn't; 'endless' trims the criticism word. 'Stick' as criticism is British idiom, as in taking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to scientism or to science's methods; the question mark signals a rather rare adjective.

clue.text: Contest unit, possibly? Certainly in an election

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether a constituency counts as a unit of competition, and saying yes at election time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with the anagram: a voter is certainly a contest unit in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in a constituency, one of the people who take part in choosing a representative.

clue.text: Almost entirely abandoning healthy food? That's unfortunate

indicators.note: abandoning means these letters are dropped from the food

parts.note: salad is the standard example of healthy food

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Nearly giving up on healthy eating is a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL less L is AL, which comes out of SALAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrettable or deplorable, as in a sad state of affairs.

clue.text: Good humour I found in cartoons, on reflection

indicators.note: reflection means the letters appear as in a mirror, backwards
found in means the letter sits inside the word

parts.note: comic strips are cartoons

explanation.surface: Someone discovers cheerfulness in comic strips after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: I in STRIPS gives STIRIPS, which reads backwards to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good or high spirits means being cheerful.

clue.text: Fellow amongst other fellows kept in reserve will have pervasive effect

indicators.note: kept in means the inner pieces go inside the outer

parts.note: ice means reserve or cold formality of manner

indicators.note: amongst means this piece sits inside the next

parts.note: other fellows are men
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by colleagues who stay in reserve will be influential everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' is coolness of manner, not a stockpile or substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being present throughout or inherent in something, a philosophical term.

clue.text: Smarten up one fellow appearing in comic

indicators.note: appearing in puts the next pieces inside the comic

parts.note: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A man spruces himself up to feature in a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dandy was a famous British weekly comic for children.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone dapper, like a dandy, is to make them look neat and fashionable.

clue.text: Nightwear sticks round me when embracing one

indicators.note: round means the outer word surrounds the rest

parts.note: jams means sticks or gets stuck

indicators.note: embracing means the word wraps itself round the next

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pyjamas cling to the speaker while hugging someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is taken literally, not as the setter's usual stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for pyjamas, clothing worn in bed.

clue.text: Unionist politician joining Conservative in project — a sudden change of view

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the outer word

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Unionist MP teams up with a Tory on a project, and the scene suddenly shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' is a verb here, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: In film editing, an abrupt cut between shots that jolts the viewer's perspective.

clue.text: Trickery disheartened school rowers

indicators.note: disheartened means the word loses its heart, leaving only its ends

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A school's rowing crew is downcast after some deception.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, as in the Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexterity used to deceive, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Religious book not polished, needing cut

parts.note: matt describes a dull, unpolished finish
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A rough holy volume needs editing.
explanation.walkthrough: MATT is the British spelling of matte.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of the four Gospels in the New Testament.

clue.text: Crows regarding instrument that's taken up

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a letter heading
a drum is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Crows taking up a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a flock of crows is a murder of crows.

clue.text: Not out circling lake or going for a stroll

indicators.note: circling means the word goes round the letter

parts.note: someone not out cold is awake, so waking
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A batter not out going round a lake on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out' sounds like cricket but means not unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on foot at a leisurely pace is what a stroll involves.

clue.text: Soldier recalling 70s war zone

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Nam is slang for Vietnam, the war that ended in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A soldier remembers the war zone he served in during the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nam is American slang for Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: A man is an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men.

clue.text: Reach toilet, being desperate — not for real?

indicators.note: desperate suggests frantic disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is frantically trying to get to the loo, or is it a hypothetical?
explanation.definitionFit: Something hypothetical exists only in theory, not in practice.

clue.text: Limited amount of stretch in old cotton cloth

indicators.note: a limited amount of these words means only a small run of their letters is used

explanation.surface: Old cotton fabric that only stretches a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A durable twilled cotton fabric used for trousers.

clue.text: Crafty copper getting pub turned over? No good

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: turned over means the word runs backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A sly policeman raids a pub, but it comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly or artful, good at deceiving to get one's way.

clue.text: Lack of welcome that is limiting college

indicators.note: limiting means the outer letters form the bounds around the next one

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cold reception that restricts entry to a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldness of manner, the frostiness of an unwelcoming reception.

clue.text: I weary the writer, recalling university old guard?

indicators.note: recalling means bringing back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to weary someone is to tire them
the writer refers to the setter, so me

explanation.surface: The retired university staff complain that they bore the author.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired professors who keep their title, academia's veterans.

clue.text: Warning about closure of line on that account

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the letter

parts.note: a threat is a warning of harm

indicators.note: closure means the end, the last letter of line

explanation.surface: A warning about closing a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the last letter of line, goes inside THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning for that reason or because of that.

clue.text: Firm's incorrect, replacing weight with stone

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: wrong means incorrect
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A company is mistaken, swapping one unit of weight for a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid and robust, as a firm structure is sturdy.
